memory_update.text: MKSI should remain in the underfollowed discovery lane for US-listed advanced packaging substrate/material exposure because Atotech maps to package substrate chemistry and electroplating, but materiality must be verified in segment disclosures.
CAMT is a yield-gate candidate rather than a substrate/material supplier; include when the funnel allows inspection/metrology bottlenecks tied to advanced packaging and HBM.
PDFS is a low-attention software/data hypothesis for advanced packaging yield orchestration; survival requires evidence of OSAT/foundry/advanced-packaging adoption and AI/HBM-specific relevance.
AMKR is best treated as a reference OSAT/customer/integration gate for the substrate/material node, not as a pure underfollowed materials candidate.

The purest substrate and material suppliers cited in the external context appear mostly non-US-listed or not clean US common-stock exposures, creating a US-listed coverage gap that pushes the discovery lane toward chemistry, inspection/metrology, OSAT, and yield software proxies.

node: Advanced packaging substrates, ABF-style insulating materials, and copper-bonding chemistry
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a US-listed discovery lane around the substrate/material chokepoint, but the best US-listed names are mostly second-order rather than pure ABF substrate makers. The most directly mapped candidates are MKS Instruments through Atotech process chemistry for package substrates and advanced packaging, Camtek through inspection/metrology tied to advanced packaging yield, PDF Solutions through semiconductor yield/data orchestration across test/assembly/packaging, and Amkor as a US-listed advanced-packaging/OSAT reference customer and capacity node. Pure substrate makers cited in external context, such as Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, Shinko, Ajinomoto, and MEC, are generally not straightforward US-listed common-stock candidates, so US-listed exposure requires accepting indirect yield-gate, chemistry, OSAT, or software/data links.
